<user_query>
[form answers] fidelity: Clickable prototype with mock data | chat: scope control (PC1/PC2/PC3 + fund always on), streaming/typing state, inline citation markers, citation drawer with the exact passage, "KB can't support this" refusal state | documents: uploaded vs generated split, per-doc status + error + Retry, Add file modal, Ingest Seeds, filters by org/status | memo reader: panel inside documents screen | api_specs: Write a fresh API_SPECS_V2 | viewport: Desktop + narrow reflow | notes: you are allowed to write an API_SPECS_V2 but it needs to make sense !
</user_query>

Decisions before writing anything:

- ONE component, three screens behind a top nav — not three files. Inline styles only.
- Type: Source Serif 4 (documents, headings, answer prose) + IBM Plex Sans (UI) + IBM Plex Mono (filenames, storage keys, markdown). Filenames in mono because the corpus has eight near-identical names per portco.
- Dashboard is Sam's morning board, not counters: Needs me (failed rows, worker errorMessage verbatim, Retry / Retry all) -> Pipeline (uploaded+seeded, status pill, passage count) -> Generated (separate list). Passage count shown because ready with 0 chunks is a lie, not a state.
- Chat: locked "Fund — always retrieved" chip so the union is never silent; inline [n] markers; drawer with the verbatim passage, heading, neighbours; refusal styled as a first-class answer in amber, not an error.
- Documents: uploaded vs generated as a hard segmented split; brief rendered as a typeset memo (fixed template headings, cited claims, evidence quotes, flags, prompt/template provenance) — never a chat bubble.
- API_SPECS_V2 = v1 plus five additions, each traced to a screen. Nothing removed, no v1 shape changes meaning, so a v1 client still works.

input.summary: v2 = v1 + 5 additions, each traced to a screen: (1) Citation.marker + [n] convention in answer text — v1's flat final list cannot say which claim a passage backs, so inline markers are unbuildable; (2) GET /chunks/:id?context=neighbors + stored heading — the drawer otherwise lands mid-sentence on overlap with no heading; (3) q on GET /documents — org+status filtering still leaves a wall of 360-feedback-2026.md; (4) sizeBytes + chunkCount on list and detail — proof of retrievability, ready-with-0-chunks surfaced as failed; (5) POST /documents/retry (batch, partial success) — seeds fail in batches. Deliberately NOT added: totals/counts endpoint, conversation persistence, websocket, generated-brief re-ingest.

Three screens (dashboard / chat / documents) + mock data modelled on the real contract: organizations fund+pc1-3, 13 uploaded docs across queued/processing/ready/failed, 6 chunks with heading+index+count, 2 generated briefs with header/sections/evidence/flags/steps/provenance. Interactions: Retry, Retry all (batch), Ingest seeds, Add file modal with .md -> 415 unsupported_media_type rejection, queued->processing->ready progression, scope chips, send + token streaming + closing citations event, citation drawer, org/status/filename filters, memo panel. Palette and type from DESIGN.md.

Implemented both, and updated the contract rather than letting UI and spec drift.

On v1's "never PC->PC": that rule conflated WHO is asking with WHAT may be retrieved. The commercial rule is the first one — a Portco Workspace user sees only their own org, enforced by identity, not by an arity limit on a parameter. This slice has no auth and one fund-side user (Sam/Hema), who is entitled to the whole portfolio; cross-portfolio search is Hema's standing question in context-brain. When auth lands the server clamps the array and 403s the rest; the wire shape does not change.

Generate stays single-portco (briefs/stream unchanged) because the memo is ABOUT one company — hence a picker at generate time instead of inheriting a possibly-multi chat scope.

<timestamp>Friday, Sep 18, 2026, 4:34 PM (UTC+2)</timestamp>
<user_query>
in the chat we have "Evidence — 4 passages, 4 documents" and the list of documents concerned, it is required in the specs?

No. SPEC Pillar 2's must is that every claim traces to a real passage you can open — the inline [n] markers satisfy it; API_SPECS only requires the closing citations event. Nothing mandates a footer.

The case for keeping it: filenames without hovering, and it is the only place a retrieved-but-unmarked passage could surface (the "uncited prose reads differently" principle in DESIGN.md). Options: remove entirely / keep the count line only / collapse behind a "4 sources" toggle.
